correctness.rationale: Two BFS tables plus rotational symmetry fix the entire shortest-path metric. Bipartite decomposition establishes two pure three-spheres and a mixed complex collapsing to either of the nine-loop neighbor complexes. The homotopy pushout of two null maps gives exactly nine two-spheres and two three-spheres at radius two. The other radii follow from graph cycle rank, the distance-four antipodal perfect matching, and diameter four. Exact independent face enumeration, chronological discrete-Morse free-face matching and mod-two boundary ranks reproduce the combinatorial input; the structural proof supplies integral homotopy, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The 16-vertex Möbius–Kantor symmetric cubic incidence graph has a canonical graph metric. Its complete, coefficient-independent Vietoris–Rips barcode and mixed two-/three-sphere homotopy type at the scale-two graph square give nontrivial natural topological information not reducible to an Euler characteristic. The distance-four perfect matching further produces a seven-sphere stage. This exact, motivated finite invariant is reusable as a structural test case without implying a general-family classification.
